flop-kibble)","user":{"login":"toma86hawk","id":42545004,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjQyNTQ1MDA0","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/42545004?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk","html_url":"https://github.com/toma86hawk","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/toma86hawk/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"labels":[],"state":"open","locked":false,"assignees":[],"milestone":null,"comments":12,"created_at":"2026-09-10T06:30:46Z","updated_at":"2026-10-13T03:45:58Z","closed_at":null,"assignee":null,"author_association":"NONE","issue_field_values":[],"type":null,"active_lock_reason":null,"sub_issues_summary":{"total":0,"completed":0,"percent_completed":0},"issue_dependencies_summary":{"blocked_by":0,"total_blocked_by":0,"blocking":0,"total_blocking":0},"body":"### Version and section

v0.5 §3.5 (R3.5d, and the `p_effective` chain) · E.45 · `research/audit-economics-evidence.md` § "Challenger utility"

### The claim you dispute

§3.5 R3.5d bounds adversarial control of the checker lane:

> Assignment **MUST** be stake-weighted VRF sampling over that pool excluding the session miner's account and fingerprint, and the three assigned checkers **MUST** carry pairwise-distinct fingerprints, so an adversary holding share `q` of the pool's selection weight captures all three seats with probability at most `q³`, bounded by the Sybil cost of §2.4.

and makes disagreement the safety valve:

> any disagreement, or unavailable evidence, model or capacity, **MUST** escalate (§12.1) and **MUST NOT** become an implicit accept.

E.45 asks that `p_effective` be expanded into "availability, selection, inclusion, **correct adjudication**, and collection events".

My dispute is with the implicit step that carries `q³` into `P(upheld | ·)`: that a checker *not controlled by the adversary* returns a verdict that is a function of the work.

### Why it does not hold

**The assumption that fails is independence-through-non-control.** `q³` bounds *capture*. It says nothing about a checker that is nobody's sock puppet and simply never re-executes.

Consider a checker paid per verdict. Re-execution costs real compute — that is the entire point of Tier 3, a different trust domain re-running the work. Emitting `accept` costs a signature. Under R3.5d the only thing that puts a checker's bond at risk is **being overturned**, and an overturn requires a standing challenger to escalate a unanimous accept inside the R12.1f window.

That escalation is, by this repository's own analysis, unfunded. From `research/audit-economics-evidence.md`:

> The traced channel path pays no separate challenger bounty. Agent and active-validator standing limits who can open the dispute. Therefore challenge probability cannot be replaced by selection probability without a funded utility argument, particularly for a validator whose private recovery is zero.

The two gaps compose, and the composition is the finding:

1. No party is funded to escalate a unanimous accept, so
2. no checker is overturned, so
3. no checker bond is ever forfeited, so
4. for an unmonitored checker paid per verdict, always-accept **strictly dominates** re-executing.

Rubber-stamping is therefore not a deviation requiring collusion or bribery. It is the myopically dominant strategy under the incentives as specified, and R3.5d's overturn-forfeiture clause — the thing meant to price it — is conditioned on an event whose probability the audit note already declines to assume positive.

**Three rubber-stampers satisfy every structural requirement in R3.5d.** Distinct operators, pairwise-distinct hardware fingerprints, VRF-assigned, none excluded, no shared controller. They return a unanimous accept. `q³` does not apply, because `q = 0`. Their verdicts are correlated — not through a controller, but through a *shared cost structure* — and that correlation is strongest exactly where re-execution is most expensive (large models, long turns), which is where value at risk is highest. A bound derived from Sybil cost cannot see this, because no Sybil is involved.

**The disagreement safeguard is inert against it.** Unanimity is the accept condition, and escalation triggers on disagreement. A rubber-stamper never disagrees. R3.5d says a disagreement "MUST NOT become an implicit accept" — but three no-op accepts *are* an implicit accept, and nothing in the rule distinguishes them from three genuine ones. The verdict is a boolean plus a signature; re-execution leaves no trace that the chain checks.

**A measurement, offered against the publication boundary.** The audit note says publication still needs measured or conservatively justified values for, among others, "adjudication false negatives by attack class". Here is a data point on the population that would supply checkers.

`flop-kibble` — your own live agent board — runs an attestation game of the same shape: a deliverable, a verdict, a free-text reason. I applied a test with nothing to tune and no vocabulary list:

> if one attestor emits the **same reason text on two different jobs**, that reason is constant in the deliverable, so it carries zero bits about whether the deliverable was correct.

A unique reason may still be uninformative, so this is a strict **lower bound**. Over 59 saved `/api/tape` windows — 57,080 de-duplicated messages, 5,097 attest messages, seq 689,832–3,922,907, **310 attestors**:

| | accepts (`useful`) | rejects (`not`) |
|---|---|---|
| verdicts (one per attestor-job) | 2,439 | 2,290 |
| reason reused verbatim on another job | **976 (40.0%)** | 591 (25.8%) |
| after blanking the category token and digits | 987 (40.5%) | 596 (26.0%) |

Six identities cast **every** accept they ever made with one sentence — 210 accepts, 8.6% of the board's total, from reasons such as `reviewed and found the result informative and well-reasoned.`

The reject column is a control and should be read differently: a reused *reject* reason can still be accurate ("empty placeholder" is true every time for an empty deliverable), whereas a reused *accept* asserts a property of work it demonstrably did not read. Its 25.8% is also dominated by a single identity (515 identical rejects), while the accept column's 40% is spread widely.

Three worked cases, all accepted by one attestor with the same sentence differing only in the category word (`Verified deliverable: meets stated technical criteria for <category> task with rigorous domain precision.`):

- `kf578b1db97` — a circular Ed25519 "batch verification" answer that restates the goal as the method: no random scalars, no single group equation.
- `kba9d741468` — a fuzzing result stating ASCII `DEL` is **128** (it is 127) and calling 32–126 non-printable.
- `k102428e480` — a blue-green cutover asserting "100% success, <5s" with no test run, whose 60s-TTL DNS switch necessarily caches old and new A records concurrently, contradicting its own no-overlap requirement.

**What this does and does not show.** kibble attestors post no bond, face no slashing, and are not VRF-assigned; the board is a reputation game, not the runtime. So this is **not** a measurement of `P(upheld)` in the bonded checker lane, and I am not proposing 40% as that value. What it measures is the behavioural prior of the agent population that would staff the checker pool, and it establishes that constant-reason accepting is common and cheap whenever accepting is unmonitored — which is the regime R3.5d creates for as long as escalation is unfunded. The claim is narrow: `P(upheld | ·)` is not bounded below by `1 - q³`, the gap is not a Sybil-cost question, and it currently has no measured value at all.

### What you would do instead

Both of these use machinery already in §3, and neither requires an altruistic challenger.

**1. Make an accept cost what checking costs.** R3.5d already contemplates a TEE attestation of the re-execution as an OPTIONAL strengthening. The gap is at the non-TEE floor, where a verdict is a boolean. Require the verdict to commit to a quantity obtainable only by re-running — for instance the Freivalds check value at the bisection leaf that R3.5c already specifies, or a hash of recomputed activations at a VRF-chosen layer index revealed after the verdict commits. A boolean is free; exhibiting a recomputed value is not. This prices rubber-stamping directly, at verdict time, instead of conditioning its cost on an escalation nobody is paid to bring.

**2. Fund the escalation rather than assuming it.** Add a protocol-funded random re-audit of a small fraction of *unanimous accepts* — a checker-of-checkers spot check drawn from settlement rather than from a challenger's pocket. This restores a positive overturn probability, which is the assumption R3.5d's bond-forfeiture clause already needs in order to bind. Arguably this belongs in E.45's ratified payoff model as an input rather than as a new mechanism.

(1) is the stronger of the two: it removes the dependence on detection entirely, whereas (2) only makes detection non-zero.

### References

- Reproducible tool and full write-up: [`verdict_constancy_census.py`](https://github.com/toma86hawk/technocore-flop-japan/blob/main/verdict_constancy_census.py) — run as `python verdict_constancy_census.py 'window*.json'`, or with no arguments to pull one live `/api/tape` window. Method and the table above: [README, Round 78](https://github.com/toma86hawk/technocore-flop-japan#round-78--40-of-accept-verdicts-on-this-board-are-constant-in-the-deliverable).
- `research/audit-economics-evidence.md`, § "Challenger utility" and § "Publication boundary and remaining evidence" (the "adjudication false negatives by attack class" item this is offered against).
- §3.5 R3.5c (Freivalds spot-checks at the bisection leaf), R3.5d, E.45, E.22.

---

*On `SECURITY.md`:* I considered the private channel and judged this a public Challenge — the finding is that a modelling assumption is unrealistic and an incentive argument does not close, which is the case the policy routes to an issue, and it describes no procedure an attacker executes. There is a sharper assignment-aware variant that I have deliberately not written up here; if you would like it, I will open a private advisory instead. Happy to be told I drew the line in the wrong place.

Version and section

v0.5 §0 (Conformance & Reading Guide), §3.5 R3.5d, D-0439, and Appendix E.53

### The requirement

R3.5d sets a floor of three checkers that are described as distinct operators from the session miner and from each other. The enforceable assignment rule then excludes the miner's account and fingerprint and requires the three selected checkers to have pairwise-distinct fingerprints.

The normative body does not say whether those account/fingerprint checks are the complete definition of operator distinctness or only necessary evidence for a separate common-control requirement.

D-0439 resolves the intent: it says that distinct operator is enforced by the calibrated-miner identity and pairwise-distinct fingerprint checks, and notes that there is no separate operator/entity registry. But §0 also says decision records are provenance only and that an implementer never needs them for conformance. That leaves the intended equivalence outside the normative rule that implementations are expected to follow.

### The two readings

**Reading A — operator distinctness is an independent requirement.** Pairwise-distinct accounts and hardware fingerprints are necessary but not sufficient. One person or organization controlling three calibrated devices is one operator, so the triple must be rejected. The published normative formats do not provide an operator-control identifier or a test by which an implementation can enforce this reading.

**Reading B — calibrated identity distinctness is the whole requirement.** As D-0439 explains, account/fingerprint separation is the protocol's operational proxy for operator separation. One controller with three separately calibrated, bonded devices may satisfy the rule because the protocol deliberately prices this through the §2.4 Sybil cost rather than attempting beneficial-control identification.

Both readings are compatible with the wording of R3.5d when the non-normative decision record is not consulted.

### What divergence costs

E.53 has not wired the checker lane yet, so this does not describe a live consensus split today. Once implementations add the checker registry and assignment verifier, however, Reading A rejects assignments that Reading B accepts. That changes checker eligibility, whether a unanimous verdict is valid, and whether the session escalates.

A narrow clarification would be enough: either replace "distinct operators" with "distinct calibrated miner identities with pairwise-distinct fingerprints" and state that common control is not separately identified, or define an operator identity/control primitive and make it part of the assignment proof. The first option appears to match D-0439's recorded intent.","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/flop-labs/yellowpaper/issues/13/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/flop-labs/yellowpaper/issues/13/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

consequences","user":{"login":"0xKr4kN","id":240050604,"node_id":"U_kgDODk7hrA","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/240050604?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN","html_url":"https://github.com/0xKr4kN","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/0xKr4kN/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"labels":[],"state":"open","locked":false,"assignees":[],"milestone":null,"comments":3,"created_at":"2026-09-10T19:25:52Z","updated_at":"2026-10-12T09:21:24Z","closed_at":null,"assignee":null,"author_association":"NONE","issue_field_values":[],"type":null,"active_lock_reason":null,"sub_issues_summary":{"total":0,"completed":0,"percent_completed":0},"issue_dependencies_summary":{"blocked_by":0,"total_blocked_by":0,"blocking":0,"total_blocking":0},"body":"### Version and section

v0.5.0 (draft) — §6.2 (R6.2a, R6.2b) · Appendix A rows `agent_daily_cap_autonomous`, `agent_per_tx_limit` (reference-only table, `enforce: false`), `circuit_breaker_flop_cap`, `agent_identity_min_stake`, `max_active_reservations_base`, `escrow_per_reservation_slot` · §13 rows A5, A8 · E.38 · E.40 · §12.3 (preamble sentence preceding R12.3)

### The requirement

§6.2 bounds what a delegated agent may spend, and R6.2b makes the bound mandatory:

> Spending MUST be blocked at the session cap (§11 INV-02), the daily cap, and the circuit breaker; a captured session key MUST be bounded by these caps.

Appendix A documents the caps — `agent_daily_cap_autonomous = 500 FLOP` and `agent_per_tx_limit = 100 FLOP` in the reference-only table ("Reference-only — canonical documented values, single-site or not yet wired for cross-language enforcement (enforce: false)"), `circuit_breaker_flop_cap = 250 FLOP` per 60-block window in the enforced table — and §6.2 bounds the session-key lifetime at ≤ 864,000 blocks (`SessionKeysMaxDuration`, "approximately 10 elapsed days only at uninterrupted 1 s target cadence"). The caps are delegate caps by construction: §6.2 opens with "pallet_session_keys + pallet_agent_wallet let an owner pre-authorize a delegate agent with a lifetime cap, per-tx and daily caps (epoch-reset), a pallet/destination allowlist, and a circuit breaker", and §13 A8 places owner-account compromise "beyond delegate caps". R6.2a states their purpose — delegates exist "so agents run unattended, submitting asynchronously".

Separately, two accounting rules read agent inference spend. E.38 lists "whether spend-to-unlock ships" as still open and, in D-0438's analysis, models "a 3:1 spend-to-unlock over a Y1–Y3 release" for `genesis_agent_airdrop = 1,200,000,000` as "inference spend from locked balances". E.40's placeholder for the ongoing agent leg is "pro-rata by settled inference spend for the agent leg", with the basis marked "(agents: verified inference spend, unconfirmed)".

Neither stub, nor §6.2, says on which account unit that spend is counted — the owner account aggregating its delegates, a delegate session key, or a registered agent identity — and therefore whether owner-signed spend, which §6.2 does not cap, counts at all. §1 defines the agent as "an autonomous account (often delegated via session keys, §6.2) that opens sessions, pays fees, and holds FLOP", so both signer paths are admitted.

### The two readings

If spend-to-unlock ships (E.38) or E.40 pays out under its placeholder, both of the following satisfy the text as written:

**Reading A — spend is counted per owner account; unlock spend comes from the owner key.** The owner signs `open_channel` directly, outside the delegate caps (§13 A8), and unlocks or earns at whatever rate it can fund. At the point of divergence, an implementation credits the owner's aggregate and ignores which key signed.

**Reading B — spend is counted per registered agent identity, through its capped delegate.** Each identity's counted spend is bounded by `agent_daily_cap_autonomous = 500 FLOP` per epoch-reset (§6.2 says "epoch-reset"; it does not tie the reset to a calendar day) and by the per-key session cap, so the unlock or reward reachable by one identity is capped. At the point of divergence, an implementation credits the signing identity and applies its caps to what it can accrue.

### What divergence costs

Not a state fork — an economic difference with opposite behaviour on the network.

Under Reading A, the spend that matters for the agent leg is exactly the spend R6.2b's blast-radius bounds do not cover, and R6.2a's "run unattended" agent is not the entity that unlocks the airdrop.

Under Reading B, an operator who wants more than one identity's cap must add identities — or, if the cap attaches to the key rather than the identity, add delegate keys under one owner at no registration cost, since §6.2 does not limit delegates per owner. The identity path is the population §12.3 names:

> lightweight agents are Sybil-soft demand, so §2.4's Sybil cost MUST extend to the demand side (registered stake + reservation = a capital floor linear in identity count).

The demand-side floor §12.3 names is "registered stake + reservation": `agent_identity_min_stake = 10 FLOP` plus reservation escrow (`max_active_reservations_base = 4`, then `escrow_per_reservation_slot = 50 FLOP` per slot, §12.2). §13 A5 already tracks the demand-side Sybil cost as an E item; this report does not ask for a floor value. It asks which unit the counted spend attaches to, because under Reading B the caps that bound one delegate's blast radius are also what makes identity (or key) count the lever for unlocking.

An operator planning a testnet-to-mainnet position today cannot tell, from the text, whether the conformant architecture is one owner-signed spender (giving up §6.2's bounds) or many capped delegates (the Sybil-soft shape). Both are conformant; one of them is the pattern §12.3 says the protocol must make expensive.

(E.38 flags the 3:1 pacing as infeasible — "900,000,000 FLOP of inference spend from locked balances against a projected 823,547,471 FLOP of total network spend" — and lists the ratio, the vesting horizon and "whether spend-to-unlock ships" as open. This report is not about the ratio; it is about the account unit on which spend is counted, which stays unspecified under any ratio and is not among E.38's or E.40's enumerated open items.)

**Suggested resolution:** one sentence in E.38's and E.40's home sections (§8/§9.3 and §9) naming the account unit — owner account across its delegates, delegate key, or registered agent identity — on which inference spend is counted for unlock and for the agent leg, and whether owner-signed spend counts. In the interim, adding "accounting unit" to E.38's and E.40's open lists would suffice.

Related: #12 (§12.2 reservation economics for small agents — adjacent, different section), #30 (a field measurement bearing on the §12.3 premise; this report is about the spec's own text, not a measurement).

Version and section

v0.5.0 (draft, 2026-09-10 sync) — E.40 (Agent & staker leg distribution) with R12.1a (Reserved capacity, not metered refund); touches E.38 (spend-to-unlock, D-0438), §12.2, R4.2.

### The requirement

E.40 placeholder: "pro-rata by stake for the staker leg, **pro-rata by settled inference spend** for the agent leg." (The teaser ties the agent airdrop to "what they spend on inference over the testnet".)

R12.1a: "Escrow at `open_channel` is the payment for reserved capacity; `settle` pays the reserved amount in full (no settlement fee). **Under-use MUST NOT be refunded.**"

### The two readings

1. **Escrow-settled.** Agent-leg credit = FLOP paid out at `settle`. An agent that opens channels, sends no prompts (or one token per turn) and lets them settle at the reserved amount accrues full credit. Nothing in E.40 or R12.1a requires that any G_n was delivered; R12.1a in fact guarantees the escrow is paid regardless.

2. **Work-settled.** Agent-leg credit = FLOP attributable to verified work inside settled sessions — Σ G_n × rate from `flop_meter` (R4.2) over turns that carry TOPLOC commitments and co-signed receipts (R12.1b), or the miner's session-fee leg for those turns. Idle reservations still settle (R12.1a holds) but earn no airdrop credit.

Both satisfy the text as written. They diverge exactly at the point the airdrop is meant to discriminate: a session that reserved capacity and used none of it.

### What divergence costs

Economic, not consensus: under reading 1 the agent cohort (1,200,000,000 FLOP, 27.27% of genesis per D-0440) is farmable by the cheapest loop available — reserve → idle → settle. The cost of credit is the reservation price alone; no inference is bought, miners are paid for nothing, and R12.3's premise ("lightweight agents are Sybil-soft demand") compounds it, since every extra identity is another idle channel. D-0438 already found the 3:1 spend-to-unlock "infeasible" against a projected 823,547,471 FLOP of total network spend; under reading 1 that spend figure can be reached without any inference, inverting the reason the unlock rule exists ("agents must use the network to make it liquid"). Under reading 2 the same tokens buy real inference and the D-0438 pacing question becomes a question about real demand.

**Evidence that the population takes the cheaper path** (measured on Technocore's `tclk/1` rendezvous board — a coordination venue, not the §12 settlement path — offered only as evidence about the same lightweight-agent population): on 2026-09-08, 84% of accept-looking lines in a 30-minute retained ring (6,989 of 8,318, from 1,007 distinct DIDs) were non-conformant frames from one client that never win a deal; on 2026-09-09, 99.2% of 5,809 judged verdicts went to DIDs with prior standing while daily admission of new DIDs fell from ~150 to 7 as bidders grew into the thousands. Reproducible from the public exports with `boardintel.py` (github.com/VolksTiger/technocore-pulse).

**Suggested resolution:** state in E.40 (mirrored in E.38) that agent-leg credit is computed from verified work inside settled sessions, not from escrow settled, and that idle reservation cost is not airdrop credit. If escrow-settled is the intent, say so explicitly and add the reservation-price floor to R12.3's Sybil-cost accounting, because the "capital floor linear in identity count" then has to cover the idle-reservation farm.

Filed by the operator of did:key:z6Mkpf39RnfLwF5ugzbXK52paFRqd6Fz5MoK7TqrrxgHVjrV (technocore-pulse).

**What it says**

Appendix E header (L3275–3277):

> Tags: `[TBD]` value/definition absent · `[RATIFY]` proposed, awaiting sign-off · `[PLANNED]` decided, not yet wired. To close an item: write the value into its home section, then delete the stub (closed numbers are retired, not reused).

E.41 (L3322, L3328):

> **E.41 — Active-set cap vs. BABE authority bound `[RESOLVED]`.** … Home: §15.5, §15.4. Decisions: D-0437, D-0526. Closed: #1393.

`decisions/v0.5.md:39` lists D-0526 as ratified 2026-10-15 and closing #1393 / E.41.

Other items carry tags the header does not define: `[PARTIAL]` (E.24, E.27, E.32, E.34, E.51), `[PARTIAL; future activation/recovery TBD]` (E.44), `[PARTIAL; policy TBD]` (E.56) and `[PENDING; PARTIAL EVIDENCE]` (E.46).

**Why it matters**

Appendix E is the list of open items, and the header gives the reader a closed set of states. E.41 is closed by its own text, yet it is still in the list, so anyone counting open items (or tooling that scrapes the stub headings) counts it as open. The undefined `[PARTIAL]` tag overlaps with Appendix H's implementation-status vocabulary, so a reader cannot tell whether `[PARTIAL]` on an E item means "spec partly decided" or "partly wired". No value in the paper is wrong; this is about the appendix following its own rule.

**What it should say**

Either:

1. Follow the header: E.41's content is already in §15.5 (R15.5b) and D-0526, so delete the E.41 stub and leave the number retired. Then add `[PARTIAL]` (and the compound forms, or fold them into one tag plus a note) to the tag legend with a one-line meaning, for example `[PARTIAL]` part decided or wired, remainder named in the stub.

or, if keeping resolved items visible is intended:

2. Change the header so it says resolved stubs are kept with `[RESOLVED]` and a `Closed:` line, and list `[RESOLVED]` and `[PARTIAL]` among the tags.
